Yes—these results include LLM approaches that use popularity prediction inside recommendation. TRAIL is the most direct match: a fine-tuned LLM for recommendation that jointly predicts short-term item popularity and generates explanations, reporting stronger popularity prediction and explainability than baselines [1]. Related work also uses popularity signals more indirectly: one method activates LLM guidance based partly on item popularity and improves accuracy especially in cold-start and long-tail settings [3], while FairLRM targets popularity bias by helping RecLLMs semantically interpret and address item-side and user-side sources of that bias, improving fairness and accuracy [8].

If you mean broader LLM recommendation rather than explicit popularity prediction, the papers differ: some use LLMs as explainable re-rankers instead of standalone recommenders [2], some generate temporal user profiles to improve recommendation quality and interpretability in certain domains [5], and one studies when LLM-generated profiles help in production, finding benefits mainly for exploratory users and also observing a popularity-attractor effect [10].
